gaps.sentence: The photographer ___ camera was damaged is claiming compensation.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' shows that the camera belongs to the photographer; 'who's' means 'who is'.

gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.

gaps.sentence: Have you got anything ___ will remove this stain?
gaps.explanation: After 'anything', 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun; 'which' is avoided after -thing words.

gaps.sentence: Mount Everest, ___ was first climbed in 1953, attracts hundreds of climbers every year.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' introduces extra information about the mountain; 'that' is wrong after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The reason ___ he resigned was never explained.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' is the fixed pattern.

gaps.sentence: The candidate ___ speech impressed us most got the job.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose speech' — the speech belonged to the candidate.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ my grandmother was born has no shops.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' is the relative adverb for places; 'which' cannot stand alone here because no preposition is present.

gaps.sentence: The lawyers, against ___ the case was brought, denied everything.
gaps.hint: the case was brought against them
gaps.explanation: 'Against whom' is the formal relative pattern; 'who' and 'that' cannot follow prepositions.
